recognize_zh: 四顆異常前骨髓細胞的核呈雙葉、摺疊或蝴蝶狀（bilobed/folded），細胞質中度嗜鹼、顆粒稀少，形態符合低顆粒型急性前骨髓性白血病（hypogranular APL, M3v）。
features: Four large atypical cells with moderate amounts of blue-gray cytoplasm
Nuclei deeply folded, creased or bilobed (butterfly/crumpled-paper appearance)
Finely dispersed chromatin; nucleoli not prominent
Cytoplasm largely hypogranular with only faint dust-like granules; irregular cytoplasmic margins with small blebs
No Auer rods or faggot cells visible in this field
Background red cells with overlapping/clustered arrangement; no normal leukocytes in view
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows four large abnormal cells with moderate, pale basophilic cytoplasm and irregular cytoplasmic outlines. Their nuclei are markedly folded, creased, or bilobed, with finely dispersed chromatin. Cytoplasmic granules are sparse and fine, and no Auer rods or faggot cells are identified in this field. Findings are consistent with abnormal promyelocytes of the hypogranular (microgranular) variant of acute promyelocytic leukemia; urgent confirmation of PML::RARA and coagulation screening for DIC is recommended.

ddx.vs: Promonocytes also have folded nuclei but show gray-blue cytoplasm with vacuoles, NSE positivity and weak MPO, whereas M3v cells are strongly MPO positive and CD34/HLA-DR negative.
Classic APL cells have dense azurophilic granules obscuring the nucleus and frequent Auer rod bundles, whereas these cells are hypogranular.
Normal promyelocytes have a round eccentric nucleus with a perinuclear Golgi zone and abundant evenly distributed primary granules, not folded bilobed nuclei.

ddx.dx: Lymphoma cells with cleaved nuclei (e.g., Sézary cells)
ddx.vs: Lymphoma cells have condensed chromatin and scant cytoplasm, lack myeloid granules, and are MPO negative with a lymphoid immunophenotype.
